standards.label: At least as likely as not
standards.plainText: A VA claim does not need proof beyond doubt. The question is whether it is at least as likely as not (a 50 percent or greater probability) that the condition is related to service. When the evidence for and against is in balance, the tie goes to the Veteran. The opinion sentence a reviewing clinician signs usually reads: "It is at least as likely as not (50 percent or greater probability) that the Veteran's [condition] is related to [in-service event, exposure, or service-connected condition]."
standards.opinionTemplate: It is at least as likely as not (50 percent or greater probability) that the Veteran's {condition} is related to {basis}.

standards.label: Benefit of the doubt
standards.plainText: When the positive and negative evidence is roughly equal on any issue material to the claim, the benefit of the doubt goes to the Veteran. A nexus opinion does not have to be stated with certainty to support the claim.

standards.label: Direct service connection (the three Shedden elements)
standards.citation: 38 CFR 3.303; Shedden v. Principi, 381 F.3d 1163 (Fed. Cir. 2004); Caluza v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 498 (1995)
standards.plainText: Direct service connection needs three things: (1) a current, diagnosed disability; (2) an in-service event, injury, or disease; and (3) a medical link (nexus) between the two. A nexus letter is the evidence that supports element three.

standards.label: Continuity of symptoms
standards.citation: 38 CFR 3.303(b); Walker v. Shinseki, 708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013)
standards.plainText: For a chronic disease listed under 38 CFR 3.309(a), symptoms that began in service and continued without a clear break can establish service connection even without a separate nexus opinion. For other conditions, continuity of symptoms is still helpful evidence that supports a nexus.

standards.label: Aggravation of a pre-service condition
standards.citation: 38 CFR 3.306; Wagner v. Principi, 370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)
standards.plainText: A condition that existed before service can still be service connected if service made it permanently worse beyond its natural progression. The letter should describe the baseline before service and the specific worsening during service.

standards.label: Secondary service connection
standards.citation: 38 CFR 3.310; Allen v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 439 (1995); Wallin v. West, 11 Vet. App. 509 (1998)
standards.plainText: A condition can be service connected if it was caused or made worse by a condition the VA has already service connected. The letter links the claimed condition to the already-connected primary condition and does not need a separate in-service event.

standards.label: Presumptive service connection
standards.plainText: For certain exposures and service locations, the VA presumes a listed condition is related to service, so a medical nexus letter is usually not required. If a condition qualifies as presumptive, the stronger and faster path is often to claim it as presumptive rather than to pay for a nexus opinion.
